newsitem.title: FRANCE: France says reforms of banking sector needed.
newsitem.headline: France says reforms of banking sector needed.

text.p: Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on Tuesday France's troubled banking sector needed sweeping reforms and the changes must be completed before introduction of the European single currency in 1999.
"French banks can no longer stay on the sidelines," he told a National Assembly panel examining the sector's plight, saying the banks lagged international rivals in profitability.
Arthuis said the banks had to be ready to meet the challenges posed by monetary union, due to start on January 1, 1999. "Reorganisation...can't wait any longer."
Arthuis said various changes were necessary, including changing a 1937 decree restricting banking hours and overhauling the Caisse d'Epargne savings network.

The Caisse has been sharply criticised by France's commercial banks, which argue that its lack of outside investors gives it no incentive to make a profit and encourages it to undercut its competitors on loans.
Arthuis suggested the Caisse should be obliged to produce a more significant return on equity.
In addition, he said, the government would look at easing the tax burden on banks. "We will consider a gradual reduction in the contribution from financial institutions," he said.

He called for better monitoring of financial institutions, citing the case of state-owned bank Credit Lyonnais whose reckless lending in the late 1980s and early 1990s cost French taxpayers billions of francs.
Arthuis added that further concentration was needed in France's segmented banking sector.

"There are too many groups (in France) compared with two or three" for other countries such as Germany, Arthuis said. He said that lack of concentration prevented banks from exploiting economies of scale.
Banks were hammered by a property crisis after they and other financial institutions invested heavily in development projects just ahead of the downturn of the early 1990s.

Arthuis said there had been some improvement in the past year linked to better cost controls and higher revenues from market activities. But he said quick action was needed as the banking system was fragile.
